column3: The Hebrew has plural “doors” and says he returns “in peace”; BSB has singular “door” and “my triumphant return”.
The Hebrew says he struck them with a very great blow and separately numbers twenty cities; BSB makes the cities the direct object of devastation.
The Hebrew does not repeat Jephthah’s name and retains the image of opening his mouth to the LORD; BSB names him and says “given my word”.
The Hebrew repeats mouth imagery twice; BSB says “given your word” and “as you have said”.
The Hebrew begins with a passive request, “let this thing be done for me”, and explicitly describes going down to the mountains; BSB uses “Let me do” and “wander”.
The Hebrew explicitly pairs “she and her companions” for going, then uses a singular verb for her weeping.
The Hebrew repeats the root for the vow and uses the image of not knowing a man; BSB says she had never had relations with a man.
The Hebrew calls them “the daughters of Israel”; BSB says “the young women of Israel”.
